This looks like late 2017. The fed funds rate is about 1.16%, which fits the Fed's range of 1.00–1.25% from June to December 2017. The unemployment rate is 4.1%, which matches October–December 2017. The VIX at 10.7 is also consistent with that period. Headline CPI at 2.05% fits October 2017, while November's would be about 2.2%. The 10-year yield at 2.37% and the 2-year at 1.78% both fit November 2017, though the 2-year was nearer 1.6% in October.

The 2-year yield rose 0.45 over three months, from about 1.33% in August, which suggests a November reading near 1.78%. The fed funds effective rate was 1.16% in November 2017 and 1.30% in December, so November fits. The 1-month US equity return of +3.1% matches November, when the S&P 500 gained about 3.1%. The 3-month change in unemployment of -0.2 also fits, since it was 4.3% in August and 4.1% in November. Gold rose 0.4% in November.

Taken together, the snapshot most likely describes November 2017.
